excerpt: Pop Meals, formerly dahmakan, is a Malaysian food brand selling affordable local meals for delivery, pickup and dine-in from its own central kitchen and outlets.
content:
Pop Meals is a Malaysian food company that cooks and sells affordable, locally popular meals through its own app, for delivery, pickup and dine-in at its outlets. Unlike a delivery marketplace, it makes its own recipes and food in a central kitchen and runs its own technology and deliveries. Its website says the central kitchen, operated by Farm To Fork Sdn Bhd, is halal-certified by JAKIM, Malaysia's Department of Islamic Development.

The company started as dahmakan, a healthy gourmet meal delivery brand. Vulcan Post reported in February 2021 that after six years it had rebranded as Pop Meals late in 2020, dropping its healthy-food image for cheaper, more popular dishes and more locations, while keeping its model of making its own food, technology and deliveries. Vulcan Post said dahmakan had raised pre-Series A, Series A and Series B funding from investors including Partech, UpHonest Capital and the Korean delivery company Woowa Brothers, and had expanded into Thailand in 2018 by acquiring Polpa. Investor White Star Capital lists Pop Meals in its portfolio. In 2023 BFM reported that Pop Meals was expanding across Southeast Asia with more than 35 smart outlets, citing Crunchbase data of about $27 million raised over five rounds.

Pop Meals does not publish a fixed price list on its website; menu prices are shown in its app and at outlets, and it promotes vouchers and rewards on orders. It is an option for people in the parts of Malaysia it serves who want cheap local food from a single brand; customers wanting many restaurants in one app use marketplaces such as GrabFood or foodpanda.

We have not used Pop Meals for this page. It brings together Pop Meals's own website and the reporting linked under Sources, and says where each fact comes from. Nothing here is paid placement.

faq.q: Is Pop Meals the same as dahmakan?
faq.a: Yes. dahmakan rebranded as Pop Meals in late 2020, Vulcan Post reported.
Its website says its central kitchen is halal-certified by JAKIM.
It cooks its own meals in a central kitchen and sells them through its app for delivery, pickup and dine-in.
Vulcan Post named investors including Partech, UpHonest Capital and Woowa Brothers; White Star Capital lists it in its portfolio.
